scope: Strict named-flower, robot-hand, and contact-pair acceptance for real flower-arranging frames 110-198
summary: The frozen 3.708-second seed-42 cabbage-route candidate passed all 56 strict gates after adding persistent named flower instances, two independent robot-hand tracks, and phase-specific image-plane contact pairs.
evidence: strict-object-gate-v2/gate-report.json records 56/56 passing gates and ALLOW_FULL_FILM_EXPANSION without lowering thresholds.
Three named flower instances and both robot hands are tracked over 89 camera-frame pixels; four phase-specific contact pairs pass visibility, p90-distance, and maximum-distance gates.
Aligned motion preservation is 0.841772, target identity is 0.981864, and temporal consistency is 0.758863.
Dense semantic review passes complete human removal, two mechanical hands, plausible contact, and named-flower identity/order preservation.
The accepted 896x512, 24 FPS, 89-frame video has SHA-256 2afd1238a976b3b87b10ebbcbccb83ac3d5e3ca630af184738bb8bb2df00f255.
lessons: A generic bouquet area proxy is not a valid substitute for persistent per-flower identity and explicit hand-to-stem contact supervision.
The original seed-42 pixels were already geometrically viable; correcting the supervision, rather than regenerating the accepted window, preserved its quality.
limitations: Only three visually separable held flowers are assigned identities; background flowers are outside this claim.
Contact is a 2-D camera-pixel mask-distance measurement, not force or 3-D tactile sensing.
The result validates one 89-frame window, not the complete 27.5-second film.
next_actions: Freeze this window and require every overlapping expansion window to pass the same human-removal, identity, contact, and temporal gates before stitching.
